symptom: SEC005 said strict mode enforces XPath constraints and is relevant to CVE-2023-23835, suggested the deprecated `ALTER PROJECT SECURITY STRICT MODE ON;`, and fired on classic-client projects where strict mode cannot be enabled
cause: the rule's rationale was written from a CVE name rather than Mendix's strict mode page; strict mode restricts the client API (data.action/create/commit/remove/rollback, data.get except by GUID) and exists only with the React client at Production level. CVE-2023-23835 is fixed by a runtime update. The suggestion was not updated when `alter app security` moved to a property list (MDL-DEPR554)
insight: A rule's remedy text is code nobody runs: pin the suggested statement in a test so a syntax deprecation breaks it. Check a security rule's rationale against the vendor's page for the setting, not the CVE it is named after — the security report had the right explanation all along, and the two had never been compared
